title: Shared i18n demo
subtitle: A lightweight React i18next wrapper with cookie persistence.

overview.heading: Overview
overview.description: @asafarim/shared-i18n ships both a LanguageSwitcher (language-only) and CountryLanguageSelector (country + language) from a single install.

features.title: LanguageSwitcher
items: Changes i18n translation language (en, nl, fr, de …)
Three variants: buttons, select dropdown, icon-dropdown
Cookie-based persistence and automatic browser detection
Use resolveLocaleFromLanguage adapter for URL-safe routing
Best for apps where country / market does not matter

selectors.title: CountryLanguageSelector
items: Carries both country AND language: { country: 'BE', language: 'en' }
Can distinguish be-en from nl-en, lu-en, gb-en
Image flags (flagcdn.com) or emoji flags
Compact, full, flag-only, and custom trigger variants
Best for localized URLs like /be-en/get-started

useCases.title: Perfect For
items: Locale-aware URL routing (Benelux, EU, global)
Enterprise platforms with country + language preferences
Apps that need to distinguish be-en from gb-en
Identity and authentication systems with per-locale content
SaaS applications serving international markets

getStarted.heading: Get Started
getStarted.intro: Everything you need — LanguageSwitcher and CountryLanguageSelector — comes from one package.

steps.title: 1. Install
steps.description: One package gives you both the language-only switcher and the country+language selector.

steps.title: 2. Import the selector stylesheet
steps.description: Add the CountryLanguageSelector CSS once in your entry point.

steps.title: 3. Initialize i18n
steps.description: Call initI18n at application startup with your translation resources.

steps.title: 4. Add CountryLanguageSelector
steps.description: Import from @asafarim/shared-i18n — no separate package required.

steps.title: 5. Add LanguageSwitcher
steps.description: For translation-only apps. Wire through resolveLocaleFromLanguage when you also have locale URLs.

steps.title: 6. GitHub Pages SPA fallback (optional)
steps.description: For static hosting on GitHub Pages, add a 404.html redirect strategy.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Use CountryLanguageSelector when your app has locale-aware URLs
Use LanguageSwitcher + resolveLocaleFromLanguage as a lightweight adapter layer
Both components are controlled — pass value={locale} and onChange to stay in sync
i18next stores language-only; the URL stores country + language
Set VITE_IDENTITY_API_URL for backend language-preference synchronization

routingContract.heading: Routing contract
routingContract.description: The URL is the source of truth for both locale and active page.
items: {base} redirects to {target}
{pattern} drives the UI
CountryLanguageSelector change → full locale update
LanguageSwitcher change → language resolved via resolveLocaleFromLanguage
Invalid slug → {defaultSlug}; invalid page → {defaultPage}

languageSwitchers.heading: Language Switchers
languageSwitchers.intro: LanguageSwitcher is language-only — it does not know which country the user is in. Each variant below is wired through resolveLocaleFromLanguage so selecting a language still produces a valid locale URL.

distinction.title: Why LanguageSwitcher cannot replace CountryLanguageSelector
distinction.p1: All four of these locale slugs carry the same language (English) but different countries. LanguageSwitcher cannot distinguish them:
distinction.p2: CountryLanguageSelector carries both country and language, so it can represent and distinguish all four.
distinction.link: See the Country Language Selectors tab for that.

variants.title: Buttons variant
variants.desc: Individual buttons for each language. Fires onChanged with a language code.

variants.title: Select dropdown — text only
variants.desc: Native <select> with language names. No emoji.

variants.title: Icon dropdown — all languages
variants.desc: Compact flag-emoji dropdown showing all supported languages.

variants.title: Icon dropdown — limited languages
variants.desc: Restricted to English and Dutch only. Useful to match the demo country scope.

variants.title: Icon dropdown — with labels
variants.desc: Same as above but shows language names alongside the flag emoji.

variants.title: Toggle button (2 languages)
variants.desc: When exactly 2 languages are provided and isToggler=true, renders a single toggle button.

languageSwitchers.note: This control changes language only. The demo maps the selected language back to a full locale via resolveLocaleFromLanguage so the URL stays valid.

routingLab.heading: Routing Lab
routingLab.intro: Side-by-side comparison of how LanguageSwitcher and CountryLanguageSelector behave when changing locale. The URL updates live.

langOnly.title: Language-only action
langOnly.desc: LanguageSwitcher fires a language code. The demo uses resolveLocaleFromLanguage to map it to a valid full locale. If the current country does not support the language, a fallback notice is shown.

countryLang.title: Country-language action
countryLang.desc: CountryLanguageSelector fires a full { country, language } object directly — no adapter needed. The URL always has the right country + language.

scenarios.title: Scripted scenarios
scenarios.desc: Click a row to apply the scenario and watch the URL and locale chip update.

countryLanguageSelectors.heading: Country Language Selectors
countryLanguageSelectors.intro: CountryLanguageSelector carries both country and language, making it the right choice for locale-aware URLs. All variants below share the same controlled locale — changing any one updates the URL and both navbar selectors.

variants.title: Image flags · compact trigger
variants.desc: Uses SVG flags from flagcdn.com — works on Windows where emoji flags render as ISO codes.

variants.title: Disabled state
variants.desc: The selector can be disabled while loading or when the user lacks permission to change locale.

variants.title: Full names · image flags
variants.desc: Shows the full country and language names — useful when space is not constrained.

variants.title: Flag-only trigger
variants.desc: Only the flag is shown in the trigger — ideal for very tight navbars.

variants.title: Custom trigger via renderTrigger
variants.desc: Full control over the trigger button via the renderTrigger render prop. Uses an inline flag image so it works on Windows.

variants.title: Popover aligned to start
variants.desc: Align the dropdown popover to the left edge of the trigger via align='start'.
